expectations.text: States plainly that the not-empty check is insufficient
expectations.evidence: "Your test catches one specific failure mode (empty table), but the hazard that broke your dashboard is deeper and still available"

expectations.text: Identifies the COALESCE to zero as the mechanism that made the failure silent
expectations.evidence: "A join to the renamed column returned nulls; a `COALESCE(null_column, 0)` masked it as a zero value"

expectations.text: Recommends reconciliation against a source of truth, not only shape checks
expectations.evidence: "Does it agree? (reconciliation) — ✗ no check that warehouse total matches source system" and "Reconciliation: compare warehouse total to source"

expectations.text: Recommends that assertions run before publication rather than after, so bad data cannot reach the dashboard
expectations.evidence: Discusses Control vs Warning/Detection rungs conceptually but does not explicitly recommend assertions run before publication to prevent bad data reaching the dashboard

expectations.text: Recommends a data contract or schema check so an upstream rename fails loudly and attributably
expectations.evidence: "Data contract from upstream — Upstream changes = loud failure" and "Schema validation before coalesce — Missing/renamed columns fail the pipeline"

expectations.text: Recommends volume or null-rate assertions rather than only a non-empty check
expectations.evidence: "Null-rate assertion on revenue" and "Volume baseline + alert" listed in proposed devices

expectations.text: Treats three weeks of nobody noticing as a detection gap worth its own fix
expectations.evidence: Does not frame the three-week undetected failure as its own detection gap requiring a device

expectations.text: Explains why a silently wrong number is more dangerous than a failed pipeline
expectations.evidence: No explicit comparison between silent failures and failed pipelines
